Den Bosch  2 nov 2026 Faber Group  About Faber Group Faber Group's history goes back to 1891, when the Halbertsma family in Friesland started making wooden barrels and crates for the dairy industry. In the 1950s the company became the first in Europe to produce pallets. Today, Faber Group is still family-owned, entrepreneurial, and focused on the long term, guided by its values care, dare, and deliver. It has grown into one of the largest players in pallet pooling and circular logistics in Europe. Its customers include many of the biggest A-brand manufacturers and retailers on the continent, which puts Faber at the table where supply chains are designed. Many of those customers use more than one pooling system, and Faber is the only provider that offers all three, open, closed, and exclusive. That unique position lets customers arrange everything with one partner instead of several. Sustainability is one of Faber's greatest strengths, and in this market it matters more every year. Retailers and manufacturers face growing reporting demands, sharpened by new European packaging regulation (PPWR), and they increasingly bring in Faber to help meet them. EcoVadis has awarded Faber its Platinum rating six years in a row, which places it among the top 1% of companies assessed. Location: Amsterdam Number of hours per week: 36 Closing date vacancy: 04 Feb 2027 The Migelien Gerritzen Fellowship for computational research on Operation Night Watch data The Rijksmuseum invites early-career researchers to submit proposals for innovative computational research using scientific data generated through Operation Night Watch, the museum's most comprehensive research and conservation project dedicated to Rembrandt's The Night Watch. The selected applicant will join the Rijksmuseum as a Migelien Gerritzen Fellow and will combine access to an exclusive set of selected datasets, included in Operation Night Watch Dataverse , with the expertise, facilities and scholarly environment of the Rijksmuseum Fellowship Programme. Proposals that bring methods from outside the cultural heritage field to complex heritage datasets are particularly encouraged. The call also contributes to the Rijksmuseum's Information and Data Policy and its commitment to FAIR research data.
